newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNITED SLUMP TO WORST DEFEAT IN 12 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED SLUMP TO WORST DEFEAT IN 12 YEARS.

text.p: Newcastle handed Manchester United their heaviest defeat in 12 years on Sunday, thrashing them 5-0 and avenging a string of heart-breaking recent losses to the English champions.
Not since October 27, 1984, when United crashed by the same scoreline at Everton, has the biggest club in British soccer been so humiliated.

Darren Peacock, David Ginola, Les Ferdinand, Alan Shearer and Philippe Albert scored a goal apiece, Shearer hit a post with a stinging first-half strike, and Alex Ferguson's side were outclassed across the board.
The win was Newcastle's first in the league over United since 1987 and marked the first time the Reds have conceded five goals since September 1989, when they lost 5-1 to Manchester City.
Prior to the 1984 loss at Everton, the worst defeat was in 1980 when United went down 6-0 at Ipswich Town in the old first division.
Sunday's scoreline avenged two hard-felt Newcastle defeats.
In last season's corresponding fixture at St James' Park a single goal from Eric Cantona gave United a tense victory which turned the course of the league championship towards the Lancashire side.

And in August this year United swamped Newcastle 4-0 in the Charity Shield league curtain-raiser at Wembley, a result which appeared to signal the champions still had the edge over last season's league runners-up.
Sunday's astonishing scoreline takes Kevin Keegan's side to the top of the premier league with 24 points, five clear of United and three ahead of London sides Arsenal and Wimbledon.
Liverpool, whose Merseyside derby against Everton was postponed because of a waterlogged pitch earlier on Sunday, are fourth on 20 points with a game in hand.
Newcastle dominated from the outset but needed a touch of good fortune to take the lead.
Twelve minutes into the match, Peter Beardsley swung in a deep corner from the Newcastle left, Shearer headed the ball across the penalty area and Peacock headed goalwards.
The ball bobbled through a forest of legs and United defender Denis Irwin scrambled it clear.
But the referee, after a brief look across to his linesman and despite furious protests from the United players, ruled the ball had crossed the line.

There was no disputing Newcastle's second, a classy strike from Ginola, back to his magnificent best after a run of poor form which has seen him dropped or substituted from Newcastle's last five games.

With half an hour gone, the Frenchman wheeled clear of England defender Gary Neville on the edge of the penalty area and -- without looking up -- slammed a right-foot drive into the top left hand corner of Peter Schmeichel's net.
Shearer hit the post as Newcastle, smarting from a midweek UEFA Cup defeat in Hungary, surged forward in a bid to kill off the game.
Their third goal came after the interval, courtesy of the blossoming Shearer-Ferdinand partnership.

Shearer ploughed down the right flank, pulled back a cross from a seemingly impossible angle, and Ferdinand's header crashed off Schmeichel's bar into the net to take his goal-tally for the season into double figures.

Shearer scored number four, pouncing on a rebound after ex-England midfielder Beardsley and Ferdinand had brought two fine saves from Schmeichel, and Albert completed United's misery with an fine lob from 25 metres.
"It's sweet revenge," Shearer said afterwards. "They embarrassed us in the Charity Shield...now we've embarrassed them. Not many teams have done that in the last five years."
But Shearer found a little charity for the club he rejected in the summer to join Newcastle.
"They never gave up and I still think the team that finishes above them will win the league," he said.

"I can't believe it," said Albert, who fought a French-language war of words with Cantona throughout the often heated match in which six players were booked. "But then I couldn't believe they beat us 4-0 in the Charity Shield."
